Local Medicare & insurance help for Falls Church

Honorbrook is an independent agency based right nearby in Tysons — just a short drive from "The Little City." That means we can help your Falls Church neighbors the way they prefer: in person by appointment, at our office or yours, or entirely over the phone if that's simpler. There's no call center and no pressure — just straight answers from a licensed local agent.

Our help is free. Because the insurance carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, you pay nothing extra for our time, and by law your premium is identical whether you work with us or enroll on your own. The only difference is that you get someone local who compares your options, explains them in plain English, and stays available after you enroll.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.
  • A list of your prescriptions and the pharmacy you use.
  • Whether you have Medicaid or get help paying Medicare costs.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Knowing Falls Church's doctors and hospitals

Falls Church is a small independent city — affectionately nicknamed "The Little City" — tucked between Fairfax and Arlington counties, with the busy Seven Corners area right next door. Because the City of Falls Church is so compact, many residents reach for care just across the line in surrounding Fairfax County neighborhoods, and the area is well served by the Inova health system. We serve both the independent City of Falls Church and the surrounding Falls Church areas in Fairfax County.

That local geography matters more than people expect. With Medicare Advantage, plans use provider networks — and which Falls Church-area doctors, specialists, and Inova hospitals are in-network can differ from one plan to the next. Before you enroll, we verify that the providers you already rely on are covered, so you're not surprised after the fact. Being close to Arlington and just down the road from our Tysons office means we know this corner of Northern Virginia firsthand.

Why your address matters: Medicare Advantage networks and plan availability differ even within the independent City of Falls Church and the surrounding Falls Church areas in Fairfax County. We check exactly what's available and in-network at your specific Falls Church address before you decide.

Common questions

Falls Church Medicare FAQ

Can I meet with a Falls Church Medicare agent in person?
Yes. We meet Falls Church residents by appointment — our office is nearby in Tysons, just a short drive away — or we can come to you. If you'd rather not travel, we handle everything by phone at a time that works for you.
Will my Falls Church-area doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on the plan's network, so we verify your specific doctors and hospitals — including Inova facilities you may use near Falls Church — before you enroll. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan there's no network: you can see any doctor or hospital that accepts Medicare.
Do you charge Falls Church residents for help?
No. Our help is completely free. The insurance carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, and by law your premium is the same whether you use an agent or enroll on your own. You get local, expert help at no extra cost.
When can I enroll or change plans?
During your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period (Oct 15 – Dec 7), or during a Special Enrollment Period triggered by a qualifying event such as moving to or within Falls Church.

One honest call can make all the difference.
